elements.program: #11 App. A item 4: 'Dark matter is conjugate matter — alive, P.R.'s core conjecture: as χ particles (x-clumping, gated self-force) or, since v2.4, as conjugate monopoles localized in momentum'; §8: 'ordinary matter's mirror-polarized cousin'; P4: 'Matter comes in x-polarized (Standard Model) and p-polarized (χ) representations'.
elements.school: Minic 2020, arXiv:2003.00318 (posted 2020-02-29) §6.2: 'The proposal here is that the dual sector (as already indicated in the previous section) should be interpreted as the dark matter sector' (lit.py FOUND). Berglund, Hübsch and Minić, arXiv:2010.15610 (2020-10-29) abstract: 'dark matter, on the other hand, comes from the degrees of freedom dual to the visible matter' (FOUND). Belgrade talk slides, 2019-09-09, slide 5: 'DUAL PARTICLES → DUAL STANDARD MODEL (HIDDEN SECTOR?)' (slide image, not code-checkable). A proposal or candidate in every paper; never derived.
elements.note: The same identification in words. In the dark-matter sections the school's dual is a doubled coordinate x̃ at the string scale with its own momentum p̃. Its dark field is the x̃-face of the same bi-local function as the visible one ('they both stem from the same bi-local function A(x,x̃)', 2212.06086 §6.4), not a separate species in the other polarization of one phase space at ħ. The wording closest to 'conjugate matter' is 2212.06086 §6.4: 'the dual particles are conjugate to the Standard Model particles in analogy with the canonical fact that momenta p are conjugate to coordinates q'. That is a field-space conjugacy induced by [x, x̃].

elements.element: E2 what conjugate or dual means
elements.program: #11 P2′, P4, P5: χ is matter in the other Lagrangian polarization of one phase space (x, p), with only ω rigid ('symplectic rigidity ≡ constancy of ℏ'); §3: 'ρ: (x,p) → (p,−x)'.
elements.school: In modular quantum mechanics: 'x≡q/λ and x̃≡p/ε measuring position and momentum in natural units' (1606.01829 §1.1, 2016-06-06; FOUND); also Minic 2020 §3 (x̃≡p/b, ab=2πħ). In the metaparticle model, where the dark-matter claims are made: x̃ is the left-minus-right zero mode ('In terms of the left- and right-moving 0-modes of the twenty-six dimensional bosonic string, one defines', 2407.06207 eq. 3.11; FOUND), with '[x,x̃]=iλ², ... [p,p̃]=0. (Also, [x,p]=iħ=[x̃,p̃].)' (2407.06207 §3.3), and the dark fields come from the shift p̃ → p̃ + φ̃ (§3.3).
elements.note: In the foundations the dual is the program's momentum at ħ. In the model the phase space is doubled (rank 4 per dimension; r3's executed check). There x̃ is conjugate to x only on the reduced (x, x̃) space and at the string scale: 'x̃/2πλ² plays the role of the variable conjugate to x' (1706.03305 §4.2; FOUND). In the full zero-mode phase space x's canonical partner stays the ordinary p. The authors present the doubled x̃ as the realization of x̃ ≡ p/ε (2407.06207 §3.2) without saying that x̃ changes status.

elements.program: #11 P4 (p-polarized χ); §12: three candidates, χ particles, X-condensate and conjugate monopoles; §11.4: 'each electrically charged x-polarized particle having a magnetically charged p-polarized analog'.
elements.school: One dual per Standard Model field: 'Thus the entire SM would have a dual SM (which we propose, describes the dark matter sector)' (Edmonds, Minic and Takeuchi, arXiv:2109.12763 §4, 2021-09-27; FOUND). A dual photon 'distinct from the dark photon of effective field theory' (2010.15610 §5). The dark sector is said to come 'from the other E8' (2307.16712 §4.3), against dark duals 'valued in the same E8 algebra' (2111.14205; 2212.06086 §6.6). No dual charges. Minic 2020 §3 calls the fields '(“electric”)' and their duals '(“magnetic”)', and adds 'There is no overcounting here'.
elements.note: A full dual Standard Model parallels §11.4's one analog per charged particle, without magnetic charge (my comparison). #11 P4 names χ but posits no dual Standard Model. The school calls its own gauging ambiguous ('There is a possible ambiguity in this gauging', 2003.00318 §5). It does not reconcile §3's 'no overcounting' with a separate dark Lagrangian.

elements.program: #11 P4, taken strictly: 'both couple universally to H; gauge forces do not cross polarizations', with kinetic mixing ε ≲ 10⁻¹³; §13 row 7 'Permanent null'. The one exception is §11.4's shared-photon form, which needs P4 restated.
elements.school: The papers do not agree. At leading order the sectors are independent: 'to first order in the fundamental length, we can treat them as independent' (2212.06086 §6.3; FOUND). Beyond that order there is a mixing term (λ⁸/L¹⁰) f[[A, Ã]]: 'This correlation becomes invisible in effective field theory, and it vanishes as either λ→0 or L→∞', then 'Note that with a particular double scaling, this term can be finite!' (2010.15610 §4). 'the usual visible photon/dark photon coupling is subdominant to this term' (§5). Hübsch and Minic 2024 (2407.06207 §5.3, posted 2024-07-03): 'below which the dark and visible matter interact as required, only gravitationally', with the decoupling energy M_SM ≃ 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV (FOUND).
elements.note: Against strict P4, the school's main line (2020–2023) differs: non-gravitational mixing of unspecified strength, non-commuting fields and a dual photon correlated with ours. One paper (2024) matches P4 at every accessible energy. It does not reconcile this with its own cited source, which keeps the correlation 'finite even in the limit of zero momenta (deep infrared)' (2010.15610 §5).

elements.program: #11 §13 row 7: 'Permanent null (both dark-sector candidates SM-decoupled; P4 strict)', killed by 'Any confirmed non-gravitational DM–SM coupling'; §12 table: χ has a 'permanent direct-detection null'.
elements.school: Minic 2020 §5: 'Like their visible particle cousins, dark matter quanta should be detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement to visible matter', and, as a conditional, 'If the quanta of modified dark matter are metaparticles, this may explain why, so far, dark matter detection experiments have failed to detect dark matter particles' (both FOUND). 2010.15610 §5: 'These type of correlations might be found in correlated events in the accelerators'. Astrophysically, 2407.06207 §3.4 proposes the correlation as the origin of a₀ ~ cH/(2π).
elements.note: No school paper predicts a permanent null. The gravity-only regime of 2407.06207 §5.3 implies none at accessible energies, but the paper does not state it as a prediction. The school's collider and dual-photon signals are the kind of coupling row 7 names as killing the program's candidates. The a₀ correlation is an observable the program does not address: #11 never mentions Milgrom, MOND or a₀. My inference: both are candidate discriminators.

elements.program: #11 §8: 'χ propagates on g (equivalence principle; Bullet-Cluster-safe)'; §7: momentum-space geometry is a massive, reciprocity-odd spin-2 field X; App. A item 10.
elements.school: After integration over x̃, both sectors sit on √−g(x), 'where we have included the gravitational background as non-dynamical' (Minic 2020 eqs. 49–50). The dual space sets G_N and Λ: 'the weakness of gravity is determined by the size of the canonically conjugate dual space, while the smallness of the cosmological constant is given by its curvature' (2010.15610 §2; FOUND). FKLM's candidates couple to the extended metric g ⊕ g⁻¹ (2104.00802, before eq. 15).
elements.note: In both, dark matter falls on the ordinary metric. The school sets Newton's constant from the dual volume and has a dual curvature term, but no massive dual graviton. The program has X, and no G_N from a dual volume.

elements.program: #11 §8: amplitude 4πα̃m_χ/(q² + m_φ²)·F(k²/μ²), 'k the incoming relative momentum': a knee at v*, delivered by X-exchange [D — mechanism; shape O]. Flag 55, pending, disputes the mechanism.
elements.school: No self-interaction model and no dependence on relative velocity: 0 of 41 papers contain 'relative velocit' (r9-sweep, code). The only potential between metaparticles is static, 'of the Friedel form e^{−αr}/r^β cos(γr)' (2212.06086 fn 31, unpublished FKLM work); the 2019 Belgrade slide 4 writes V(r, r̃), which depends on the dual separation r̃ (slide image). The form the school gives is fuzzy: 'However, the visible φ and invisible (dark matter) φ̃ do not commute. Therefore, one could say that dark matter is fuzzy from the point of view of classical spacetime.' (2407.06207 §3.3; FOUND). 2109.12763 §6.2 assumes collisionless dark matter.
elements.note: Nothing resembles the velocity gate. The fuzzy form is nearest the program's wave branch and X-condensate, and is related to them only. A potential that depends on the separation in the dual coordinate is the school's only interaction with a momentum-like argument, and it does not depend on velocity (my reading).

elements.program: #11 §12: conjugate monopoles, 'magnetically charged topological solitons of the p-polarized sector, localized in momentum'; §11.4; App. A item 5.
elements.school: No magnetically charged or dyonic matter in any school paper read; 'monopol' occurs only in analogies and reference titles. Nearest: worldsheet dyons, whose 'Dirac-Schwinger-Zwanziger quantization of the dyon charges is equivalent to satisfying the diffeomorphism constraint' (1307.7080). The heterotic Ẽ8 'as the Langlands dual, E8∨ ..., i.e., the electro-magnetic dual', with 'Being simply laced, E8∨≈E8, and they are physically indistinguishable' (2111.14205; FOUND). 'The dual spacetime x̃ is associated with conserved dual (magnetic) charges in the same context' (2407.06207 §3.5 fn 11).
elements.note: The school's magnetic language is algebraic or at the level of gauge groups. Nothing is localized in x̃ or in momentum. The outside search (r8) found no such objects either.

elements.element: E9 vacuum and the choice of polarization
elements.program: #11 §3: 'This program's addition is to read it as spontaneous breaking, with η as the order parameter'; P2′: η = HJ 'with the real structure J chosen spontaneously'; P5: 'The vacuum selects a polarization; ours is x-tilted; the mirror vacuum is equally lawful.'
elements.school: FKLM 2021 (2104.00802, posted 2021-04-01): 'The symmetry breaking happens at the level of the vacuum sector, and thus a choice of ground state fixes a value of δ', and 'We now propose that the expansion of the Universe can act as a mechanism that selects the decoupling frame'. Both follow 'the dual symmetry is fundamentally broken at the quantum level' and 'the dual Lorentz action is not a canonical transformation'. BHM 2022 (2212.06086 §4.3): 'O(1,d−1)₂ is effectively spontaneously broken'. FLM 2016 (1606.01829 §2): 'The space U(d)/O(d) represents the choice of inequivalent lifts η'. The other choice is available: 'there is nothing special about the x^μ; we could have taken any linear subspace, such as x̃,p' (1812.10821 §2). All FOUND.
elements.note: Published before the program: a vacuum-level fixing of which coordinate serves as spacetime, the words 'spontaneously broken' for the group tied to that choice, the coset of η-choices, and the mirror choice as equally available. Not published: an exact, ω-preserving ρ broken by the vacuum, with η as order parameter, a potential, a Goldstone angle and the K-sign lock. No school paper writes a potential, an order parameter or a Goldstone mode for the polarization.

elements.program: #11 §10: τ is hilltop quintessence on the Maslov circle, 'strictly w ≥ −1; thawing corridor wₐ ≈ −1.5(1 + w₀)'. Dictionary: 'Dual stiff ↦ Λ; dual Λ ↦ stiff; dual curvature ↦ negative dark radiation'. Founding supposition 9 (C5) keeps a route through dual stiff ↦ Λ.
elements.school: At leading order Λ comes from the dual curvature: 'the smallness of the cosmological constant is given by its curvature' (2010.15610 §2). Dynamical variants have given both signs of 1 + w: 'this rules out quintessence models of an accelerating Universe with −1<w_eff<−1/3' (2202.05266, 2022). Hur et al. 2025 (2503.20854), first model: 'Clearly, w(a)<-1 for all a', and 'so this model is clearly disfavored'. Second model: 'w(a)≥-1 in all cases', with wₐ < 0, matched to the DESI DR2 maximum-likelihood points (eqs. 76–79; FOUND). No contracting dual universe drives our acceleration.
elements.note: The mechanisms differ: infinite-statistics quanta in a dual-energy band whose cutoffs move with the scale factor, against hilltop quintessence. Hur et al.'s second model shares row 4's sign pattern. At its four DESI points wₐ/(1 + w₀) = −3.02, −3.83, −3.27 and −3.47, against the corridor's −1.5 (checks.out A, my computation), which tells the two apart. The two treatments also assign the dual curvature term oppositely: our Λ in the school, negative dark radiation in #11 §10.

It is in writing from 29 February 2020 (Minic 2020 §5, §6.2), and its clearest abstract statement is Berglund, Hübsch and Minić (October 2020). propositions.id: P2 their sector correlated with ours
propositions.reason: 'Correlated' is the school's own word, and in Minic 2020, BHM 2021 and BHM 2023 it covers couplings beyond gravity: a Berry-phase-like term, mixing terms 'invisible in effective field theory' that can stay finite under a double scaling, fermion mass mixing, a dual photon correlated with ours and accelerator events. Against the program's gravity-only sector the contrast holds for these papers. The same papers treat the sectors as independent to first order in the fundamental length. Hübsch and Minic 2024 state that below about 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV dark and visible matter interact 'only gravitationally', as P4 requires at every accessible energy. So the school is not consistent on the point, and the record nowhere mentions the 2024 sentence. The MDM correlation through a₀, which the school cites as observed, is a relation between mass profiles. Its own authors allow that ΛCDM might reproduce it by gravity, while arguing that it does not.

propositions.reason: Before September 2026 the school's published work meets the program at several points beyond C1, and the record cites few of them. (1) The hard core's spontaneous reading, P2′ and P5. η is the 'polarization metric' that separates spacetime-like from momentum-like directions (FLM 2015; Minic 2020). The η-choices compatible with ω and the vacuum form U(d)/O(d) (FLM 2016). The bi-Lagrangian split is absent from the formulation and present in solutions (FLM 2014). A breaking tied to the polarization sits 'at the level of the vacuum sector', and cosmic expansion selects the frame (FKLM 2021). The same group is called 'effectively spontaneously broken' (BHM 2022). None of this is an exact ω-preserving ρ with an order parameter and a potential. (2) The compatibility theorem's positive-H form (FLM 2016). (3) The commutator-preserving inverse rescaling behind a·ã = 1, at ħ for a cell (FLM 2016; Minic 2023) and tied to cosmic expansion on x̃ (FKLM 2021); also Ṽ ∼ V⁻¹ (BHM 2019) and δx δx̃ ∼ λ² (Hur et al. 2025). (4) A dual-spacetime dark energy with row 4's sign pattern (Hur et al. 2025), beside phantom predictions from the same group, and an opposite assignment of the dual curvature term. (5) Locality tied to the choice of polarization (FLM 2016–2017), the premise of #11 §3's mandatory breaking. (6) The mirror polarization as equally lawful (P5's second clause). (7) An E8 Langlands, electric–magnetic pairing for gauge groups, and the remark that Born geometry 'also involves S-duality' (C4, §11.3). (8) A conditional explanation of dark-matter nulls with the shape of C3's argument, and a gravity-only regime below 10¹⁴ GeV (row 7). (9) Curved momentum space with its own gravity (App. A item 10). C2, C7 and the gate are absent.

overlaps_beyond_c1.note: δ fixes which commuting combination, x or x + αx̃ + …, serves as spacetime, and the essay joins this to dual degrees of freedom as candidates for 'dark matter/energy', with class II states 'being remnants'. Limits: the broken symmetry is the non-compact dual Lorentz group of the doubled (x, x̃) space at λ² = ħα′. dissent:
1. Minic 2020 §3's 'magnetic' duals. r9-sweep-verify says the paper does not say that the §3 duals are the later dark-matter fields; r1-priority-verify says §3 ties them to §5. I re-read the source (lit.py text 2003.00318). §3 says 'the dual momenta p and p̃ ... lead, via the canonical minimal coupling prescription, not only to the usual fields φ but also to their duals φ̃ (see section 5)', and eq. (22) names them '(“magnetic”) duals'. The tie to §5's dark fields is therefore in the paper, by cross-reference. I side with r1-priority-verify. r9's caveat stands: §3 says the chiral formulation adds no degrees of freedom, and nothing is magnetically charged.

2. a·ã = 1. I label the school's inverse rescaling a close variant. That is stronger than r9-sweep-verify's 'structurally analogous ... not the same thing' and findings.json's 'kinematic analogue'. My reason: FLM 2016 §1.4 performs the ω-preserving squeeze (x, x̃) → (ax, a⁻¹x̃) in one phase space at ħ, and FKLM 2021 ties the dual side's inverse scaling to the cosmological scale factor through g ⊕ g⁻¹. What differs is the use (a decoupling limit) and the interpretation (no conjugate universe derived from ω-rigidity as a cosmological law). This is a judgment, labeled as mine.

3. C5's 'not found'. That FKLM 2021 eq. (16) and BHM 2022 §4.3 and §5.3 meet part of the 'partner's identity' element is my inference; no reader or verifier argued it. It would not change C5's verdict. It would move what is unfound to the contraction as the driver and the kept route.

4. P2. r3-gravitized-verify calls the summary's wording 'faithful to the school'; r9-sweep-verify says it 'understates the overlap'. I hold that both are partly right. It is faithful to the main line of 2020–2023. As a stated difference from the program it needs the 2024 qualification, which both verifiers agree the record lacks.

5. Compatibility theorem. I label FLM 2016 §2 'same' for the statement, following r6-foundations-verify's refutation of the reader. The verifier also notes that FLM assert the 'exactly' direction in group form without proof, so the block proof stays the program's. A stricter reader could call it a close variant.

6. 2104.00802. I follow r7-vacuum-verify: 'the symmetry is restored as one goes back in time' concerns the Lorentz symmetry of dispersion relation (17), not the dual symmetry, and the vacuum-sector breaking is of a non-canonical symmetry. I read r9-sweep-verify's use of the same sentence as describing the cosmological frame, so the two do not conflict on substance. I do not adopt r9-sweep's reader's 'spontaneous in substance'.

7. Limits of my re-reading. I did not re-read the Belgrade slide images: the talk's date and wording rest on r1-priority and its verifier (file metadata, slide crops), and I rest only priority and a 'related' label on them. The Yargic thesis and JPCS 804 passages I re-read in the verifiers' text extractions of the PDFs; neither is code-checkable.
